entries.author: Peter Forbes
entries.text: The word “rumour” <8052> is elsewhere translated, amongst other things, “tidings” 1Sam 4:19 . Whilst we might think of a “rumour” as being some information of a doubtful nature this is clearly not so of the message Obadiah gave.

entries.author: Peter
entries.text: The Bible has much to say against pride, which has to be the most dangerous of all human emotions, and the most anti-God of all the things that we have and do. Humility, the opposite of pride, is the requirement of all those that are to be saved. Pride is something we must fight in all its guises.

entries.author: Peter Forbes
entries.text: Pride was not the sole domain of the Jews. Pride in her own ability was Edom’s downfall. Being a great grandson of Abraham - Gen 25:25 - the Edomites must have been instructed in the things of God because this is how Abraham worked – Gen 18:19

entries.author: Peter Forbes
entries.text: It would appear from what the prophet is saying that Edom is going to be totally destroyed, not even a little remnant remaining.

entries.author: Peter Forbes
entries.text: The “things of Esau” include the perpetual hatred – Eze 35:5 - of Israel.

entries.author: Peter Forbes
entries.text: The sentiments of this verse are seen in Joel 3:19

entries.author: Peter Forbes
entries.text: The way that Edom rejoiced over the destruction of Jerusalem is appealed to in Psa 137:7

entries.author: Peter
entries.text: The pride of Edom having been condemned, we now move on the tell of the joy that was to be enjoyed by those whose pride is abased. Obadiah reads as a very dour and negative sort of work until this point, but the last 5 verses contain real hope for Israel.

entries.author: Peter Forbes
entries.text: In saying that ‘Jacob shall possess their possessions’ the prophet is speaking of the supremacy of Israel over Edom. An aspect of this can be seen as being fulfilled when Christ returns – Zech 12:6

entries.author: Peter Forbes
entries.text: God pours out judgement upon Edom for her sins and opposition to Israel. However the end point is clear ‘the kingdom shall be the Lord’s’. We do well to remember that our God will fulfil His purpose whatever men might think.

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: The prophecy of Obadiah is against Edom - who is Esau. Edom had a perpetual hatred against Israel Ezekiel 35:5 even though he was his brother. Israel had been instructed to not meddle with Edom Deuteronomy 2:5 when they were entering the land of Canaan. However, despite this Edom had always been antagonistic to Israel. Hence the judgement through Obadiah.

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text:
I commented, when we looked at Jeremiah 49 that Jeremiah quoted the words of Obadiah. It has been suggested to me that Obadiah and Jeremiah were contemporary. Can anyone provide Biblical evidence to show this? I have tried to find support for this idea by asking brethren with no success as yet.
Edom was told 'thou shouldest not …' indicating that Edom rejoiced over the calamities that God brought upon Judah. Just because the judgement is from God we cannot presume to rejoice at the suffering that flows. Nor should we rejoice over a brother who has fallen. We might say we do not rejoice - but sometimes we are inwardly satisfied because we feel that the brother deserved to fall. We should think carefully how we think of our brethren especially when they have problems and fall short of the high calling in Christ.

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: That the house of Jacob would be a fire will be fulfilled ( Zechariah 12:6 ) when the kingdom is established.

generalEntries.author: John Wilson
generalEntries.text: Obadiah 19 . This verse points forward to the day when Israel, in its entirety will be given the land of Cannon, as promised to Abraham. The country will stretch from; SOUTH: “They of the south” The area given to Simeon, Issachar, and Zebulun. EAST: “The plain of the Philistines” The maritime border of the land with access to the sea. NORTH: “The fields of Ephraim and Samaria” The country of the Northern Kingdom. WEST: “Gilead” The land on the other side of Jordan.

generalEntries.author: Michael Parry
generalEntries.text: Obadiah means Yahweh's servant . His prophecy is essentially against Edom. Jeremiah also has a prophecy against Edom ( Jer 49:7-22 ). It is difficult, though, to place these two prophets as contemporaries with certainty. Jeremiah prophesied about 627-585 BC. Obadiah's time could place him earlier than Jeremiah at around 841 BC; or, alternately, contemporary with him at around 586 BC. One of the LORD's complaints against Edom is that they stood by in glee as they watched Jews being deported to Babylon ( vs.11,12 ). Some commentators suggest that the Edomites actually aided the Babylonians. It is not certain which deportation is being mentioned; the first in 598 BC, or the second in 587 BC. If it were the second deportation, and Obadiah prophesied in 586 BC, then he could have been an eye-witness like Jeremiah.

generalEntries.author: David Simpson
generalEntries.text: There are 3 parts to today’s short book: Obad 1:1-9 speak of Edom’s trust in Petra and it’s impenetrable rock fortress being brought to nothing. They will fall. Then Obad 1:10-16 give a reason for their downfall. They rejoiced in Israel’s punishments. Finally Obad 1:17-21 speak of Israel’s resurrection, and their triumph over Esau’s land.

generalEntries.author: Michael Parry
generalEntries.text: People from the Negev will occupy the mountains of Esau (v.19). The Nabataeans, who were Arabs from the south ( Negev means south in Hebrew), attacked and moved the Edomites out of their territory in the fifth century BC. The survivors took up refuge in Idumea, a region southeast of the Dead Sea. The Herods, who played a significant role in Christ's time, were Edomites from Idumea.

generalEntries.author: Michael Parry
generalEntries.text: Of the four major Old Testament invasions of Jerusalem, the Edomites could have been involved in two of them. The first one, which also involved the Philistines, occurred in Jehoram's reign (848-841 BC). The second was the Babylonian invasion (605-586 BC). It is not certain to which invasion Obadiah is referring, hence the difficulty in ascertaining the time of his writing.

generalEntries.author: Michael Parry
generalEntries.text:
The first fourteen verses relate to the deeds that Edom did against Jerusalem. Edom is indicted for standing by without helping while Jerusalem was being attacked (v.11); rejoicing over Judah's captivity; participating in ransacking the city (v.13); and set up posts to prevent anyone from fleeing the city (v.14).
The last seven verses (vs. 14-21) seem to be prophecy yet to be fulfilled. Edom has become a metaphor for any nation that is in opposition to Israel. And so, these verses seem to point to the end-time invasion of Israel by those nations who will seek to destroy her (see discussion on Eze 38). These nations will be destroyed and Israel will flourish when Jesus sets up His kingdom.

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: The way in which Edom exalted herself is rather like what the men wanted to do when they built the tower of Babel – Gen 11:4

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: The mention of grapegatherers is echoed in Jer 49:9 when speaking of Edom

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: The statement that God had made Edom small among the heathen – a comment on their attitude to Moab – demonstrates the truth that the Most High rules in men’s kingdoms. Dan 4:17

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: Our lives consist of things which can be seen by others and things which we would rather keep secret. In the same way that Esau’s (Edom’s) hidden actions and thoughts are seen by God our whole life is laid bare before God.

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: Jeremiah – Lam 4:21-22 – speaks ironically about this evil behaviour of Edom. They were to be taken captive by the Chaldeans

generalEntries.author: Rob de Jongh
generalEntries.text:
Judgment on Esau
The book of Obadiah contains a single chapter of 21 verses. It concerns the nations of Israel and Edom, which are the descendants of two brothers, Jacob and Esau, as you can see in v18 . Edom's sin, for which she is judged here, is outlined in v10-14 . For this treachery against his brother, Esau would be left without descendant ( v18 ).

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: The concept of punishment returning on the head of the one instigating the sin is seen often in Scripture 1Sam 25:29, 1Kin 2:32, 2Chron 6:23, Neh 4:4, Psa 7:6, Eze 17:13, 33:4, Joel 3:4,7

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: the way in which those who ate bread with Edom now “laid a wound under thee” speaks of Edom’s “friends” being treacherous.

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: there are a number of links between he prophecy of Obadiah and Jeremiah 49. Here is another one “hidden things sought out” echoes Jer 49:10

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: Man can have such a high opinion of himself and his achievements. Indeed there are times when man’s achievements are great. However he does well to remember that the Creator is supreme and knows and understands more than man ever can. This truth should impact on the way in which we think. Our knowledge is limited. No matter how astute we are. Humility before the majesty of God is essential.

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: Pride always elevates one’s opinion of one’s status. Not a godly attribute. We should actually think of others as better than ourselves. Phil 2:3 . This is the true antidote to human pride.

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: the casting lots over Jerusalem by Edom is seen with respect to the people in Joel 3:3

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text: The prediction of the prophet here is seen fulfilled in the later prophet who spoke against Edom – Jer 49:7

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text:
It was pride that was the downfall of Nebuchadnezzar. God left him to pursue his objectives until he said “is not this great Babylon that I have built” – Daniel 4:30. Pride is so dangerous and so insidious. It is only pride that causes one individual to think of himself better than another or in extreme cases better equipped than God himself.
Before we think that we would never elevate ourselves above God consider your attitude to the written word of God. Is it, without question, the guide in your life? Or do you think that there are other sources equally valuable? Or worse still do think at times that scripture teaching needs to be modified in the light of current situations?

generalEntries.author: Peter Forbes
generalEntries.text:
there were many times when nations were proud of their own perceived status in the world. Often that pride emanated from one individual who felt that it was due to their endeavours that they were great.
Edom – which is Esau historically despised God’s promises. So Edom’s fate was certain despite their pride.
